projects.title: Little Worlds
projects.tagline: A tiny living ecosystem with a life of its own.
projects.description: Little Worlds is an interactive, New Zealand-inspired ecosystem sandbox. Observe kiwi, wētā, rats, stoats and human settlers as weather, vegetation, predator–prey relationships and human decisions reshape a miniature world.
overview: Inspired by the idea of a digital terrarium, Little Worlds lets you watch a small ecosystem develop over time or intervene to see what happens next. Animals search for resources, reproduce and interact while plants, soil, weather and fungi shape the conditions around them.

The simulation draws on familiar Aotearoa New Zealand species and ecological challenges. Introduced predators, human settlements and conservation efforts can affect the balance of the world, turning small decisions into wider consequences.
The browser edition is a self-contained sandbox: each visitor explores their own ecosystem, with local saving and JSON import/export. It is not yet a single shared, continuously running world.
highlights: An evolving ecosystem with kiwi, wētā, rats, stoats and human settlers
Changing weather, vegetation, soil conditions and interconnected food webs
Creature inspection, including individual details and illustrated species cards
Environmental controls and conservation interventions
Human settlements and their effects on surrounding habitats
Population and ecosystem history charts, an event journal and clickable ecological alerts
Resizable panels, a collapsible dashboard and local saves with JSON import/export
projects.notice: Experimental educational sandbox, not a scientifically calibrated ecological model. Each visitor has a separate browser-based world.

projects.title: Design Shift
projects.tagline: One idea. A new perspective.
projects.description: A free, browser-based design-thinking challenge studio. Practise explaining an idea to different audiences by choosing what must survive, what offers useful context and what can be removed, then prototype, reflect and improve.
projects.imageAlt: Design Shift cover featuring the three essential meaning categories: Must survive, Useful context and Can remove
overview: Design Shift turns audience-centred communication into a hands-on challenge. Each brief pairs a topic with an audience and a communication format, helping learners start with people's needs rather than a preselected solution.

Work through the design-thinking stages of Empathise, Define, Distil, Prototype and Test. Decide which details matter, create an explanation and explore how the same idea changes when told to another audience.

All responses and history are stored locally in your browser, with no accounts or API keys. Optional JSON backups let you move work between browsers. Scoring is a transparent practice checklist, not an AI judgement of creativity or factual accuracy.
highlights: 20 curated topics, 12 audience lenses and 10 communication formats
Five-stage, audience-centred design-thinking practice
Sort information into Must survive, Useful context and Can remove using drag-and-drop or buttons
Contextual I'm stuck coach with reflective prompts for each stage
Try the same topic with another audience or format and compare attempts
Offline formative scoring with category breakdowns and suggestions
Local browser history, searchable attempts and Markdown/JSON export
Responsive interface; free and without sign-in or API keys
projects.notice: The practice score measures completion and suggested audience priorities, not creativity or factual accuracy. History remains on each visitor's device; use a JSON backup to move it.

projects.title: LUMIN
projects.tagline: A living atmosphere shaped by the weather outside.
projects.description: LUMIN is a browser-based generative artwork featuring a luminous artificial organism that responds to real-world weather, remembers environmental exposure, and develops a distinctive anatomy over time. Created through a five-version AI development challenge, it combines interactive digital art with weather-driven behaviour and persistent local identity.
projects.imageAlt: Glowing violet translucent alien organism surrounded by soft light on a deep navy background, with the title LUMIN
overview: LUMIN began as an experiment in creating the impression of digital life. Rather than displaying weather through ordinary charts and icons, it translates atmospheric conditions into the motion, colour, structure, and behaviour of a luminous organism.

Open-Meteo weather data influences its immediate responses to temperature, wind, precipitation, humidity, cloud cover, and daylight. Environmental summaries and a persistent organism seed give each visitor's organism a history that can shape its longer-term characteristics.

Visitors can interact with the creature using mouse or touch, inspect its internal states in the Observatory, or enter a separate Weather Laboratory to experiment with imagined conditions without changing their real-weather history.

Five successive versions were developed for a head-to-head AI-building challenge. Feedback and screenshots prompted a shift from an abstract radial visualisation toward a layered, asymmetric organism with tissue, luminous chambers, vascular circulation, and branching appendages. The development report records both successful changes and abandoned directions.
highlights: Full-screen interactive generative organism with responsive motion
Real-world weather integration through Open-Meteo
Persistent environmental history and identity-dependent anatomy
Layered translucent-looking tissue, internal luminous chambers, and circulation effects
Interactive mouse and touch reactions, plus autonomous behaviour
Weather Laboratory for manual environmental experiments
Observatory displaying behaviour, environment, and adaptation
Eco, Balanced, and Ultra quality settings
Local save, import, and export with no required account
Five-version AI development competition documented in an accompanying report
projects.notice: LUMIN runs in the browser and uses Open-Meteo for current weather. Personal organism data is stored in this browser; a new device or browser may start with a different organism. Live data requires internet access. Development report: https://dvexperiments.github.io/LUMIN/report/

projects.title: Nimlets
projects.tagline: Little lives. Big questions.
projects.description: Nimlets is a retro-inspired virtual pet game and artificial-life experiment. Hatch and care for a Nimlet, watch it develop its own personality, habits and memories, and discover how a small simulated creature can begin to feel surprisingly alive.
projects.platform: Browser (desktop and phone) / Windows desktop / Python + pygame-ce
projects.imageAlt: Nimlets pixel-art-inspired virtual pet displayed inside a retro digital companion, representing an artificial-life experiment
overview: Nimlets reimagines the simplicity of classic virtual pets. Hatch an egg, feed your Nimlet, play short mini-games, clean its room, care for its health and help it rest. The experience is designed for quick visits rather than complicated management, with one creature at the centre of the screen.

Each Nimlet has its own personality, preferences and habits. It can wander around its room, investigate familiar objects, interact with its bed, bowl and toy, respond to the cursor, and occasionally seek or avoid attention. Small memories and autonomous behaviours are intended to make the relationship feel personal rather than purely button-driven.

Nimlets grow through egg, baby, child, teen and adult stages, branching into different forms depending on care and development. Colours are randomised at hatching, while later generations and a collection of discovered forms encourage replayability. Real-time ageing, offline progression and adjustable time-speed controls let players experience the lifecycle at their own pace.

Beyond its everyday care loop, Nimlets is an ongoing exploration of artificial life and reciprocal interaction: what happens when a digital creature remembers the player, develops communication signals, experiments with its environment or initiates activities of its own? The project uses these ideas to invite questions about learning, agency, identity and what makes something appear alive.
highlights: Original pixel-art virtual pets with distinct life stages, expressions and animated behaviours
Simple care actions including feeding, playing, cleaning, medicine, training and sleep
Autonomous wandering, resting, curiosity and interactions with room objects such as a bed, bowl and toy
Cursor awareness, petting reactions, return greetings and occasional independent surprises
Hidden personality traits, favourite activities, simple memories and changing habits
Branching evolution paths, rare adult forms and individual colours randomised when an egg hatches
New generations, inherited tendencies, evolution records and a creature discovery collection
Three short mini-games with multi-round challenges and gameplay consequences
Customisable interface colour themes, pet reset and main-screen time acceleration
Automatic local saves, JSON persistence and capped offline time progression
An expanding artificial-life direction exploring communication, player prediction, experimentation and creature-led interactions
Plays in any modern browser, on a phone or a computer, and can be added to a home screen like an app; also a lightweight offline Windows build
projects.notice: Nimlets plays in the browser at https://dvexperiments.github.io/Nimlets/ on computers and phones, and can be added to a home screen. A Windows build (Nimlets.exe) is on the GitHub Releases page. Features involving deeper reciprocal learning, self-directed experiments and awareness of simulation boundaries are ongoing development goals and may not be available in every build. Creature behaviour is simulated; it is not evidence of consciousness.

projects.title: NZ EcoSim
projects.tagline: Build an island. Watch an ecosystem change. Discover the consequences.
projects.description: NZ EcoSim is an interactive Aotearoa New Zealand island ecosystem simulator. Generate a unique landscape, introduce wildlife and people, and explore how predators, conservation, climate and human decisions reshape the natural world.
overview: Begin with a procedurally generated island inspired by Aotearoa before human settlement. Choose a North or South Island setting and customise the terrain, forests, wetlands, mountains and rainfall. Then observe the world unfold, introduce species, or intervene directly.

Native birds, introduced predators, plants, soil life and marine ecosystems interact across the island. Species have different life histories, breeding patterns and ecological roles. Population crashes, predator pressure, habitat loss and conservation efforts can trigger wider changes that the simulation explains through alerts, charts and a live food web.

Human settlers form clans, build villages, gather resources, farm, fish, migrate and sometimes compete over land and food. Their choices can change habitat, spread introduced species and affect both wildlife and other settlements. Players can respond with predator traps, protected sanctuaries, habitat restoration and marine reserves.

Explore structured conservation lessons, follow individual creatures or clans, examine the island's ecological history and export classroom reports with charts and CSV data. Alternatively, leave the island running as an open-ended sandbox and see what emerges.
highlights: Procedural island generator with North/South Island settings, terrain options and adjustable rainfall and forest cover
Native New Zealand wildlife, introduced predators, plants and soil organisms with simulated lifecycles and interactions
Dynamic food-web visualisation showing feeding relationships, predator impacts and ecological cascades
Human clans that settle, build, farm, fish, trade resources, migrate and sometimes go to war
Marine ecology with fish, plankton, shellfish, seals, penguins, overfishing and marine reserves
Conservation actions including predator traps, fenced sanctuaries, revegetation and pest removal
Five guided ecological challenges, with goals and end-of-lesson debriefs
Clickable alerts explaining ecological events, likely causes, possible responses and related Aotearoa context
Population charts, historical timelines, ecosystem-health summaries and extinction reports
Creature inspection, follow camera, zoomable maps, multiple ecological overlays and custom species creation
Exportable classroom reports in PDF and CSV formats, including event, population, death and food-web data
Automatic local saving and a limited catch-up simulation with a welcome-back report
projects.notice: The README describes a Windows desktop application built with Python, Pygame and NumPy. Python is required to run the source version; a Windows executable can be built separately. Any GitHub Pages link may be a project website rather than a browser-playable version. This is a simplified interactive ecosystem model, not a validated predictor of real-world conservation outcomes.

projects.title: Ripple Map
projects.tagline: Everything is connected.
projects.description: An interactive systems-thinking lab. Reveal the invisible infrastructure, people, information, governance and ecological relationships behind everyday technologies, test disruptions and build your own systems map.
projects.imageAlt: Ripple Map network diagram illustrating interdependent infrastructure, people and ecological systems
overview: Ripple Map transforms a seemingly simple technology or public service into a layered network of interdependent supporting systems. Learners progressively reveal physical infrastructure, technology, data, people, governance and ecological resources, then inspect why each relationship matters.

Seven guided investigations—from AI services and EV charging to urban water, telehealth and satellite navigation—invite students to locate critical dependencies, explore reinforcing feedback loops, and simulate hypothetical ripple effects through a simplified dependency graph.

Students can drag elements, add their own hypotheses and connections, reflect on stakeholders and uncertainty, and export portfolio-ready Markdown notes, SVG maps or PNG images. There are no accounts or API keys.
highlights: Seven curated technology and infrastructure networks
137 system elements with 155 explained links
Six lenses: physical infrastructure, technology, data, people, governance and ecology
Visual interactive map with drag, pan, zoom, node details and keyboard-accessible inspection
21 hypothetical disruption scenarios with dependency-impact tracing
Illustrative feedback loops with explanations
Add missing elements and propose your own relationships
Guided systems-thinking reflections and contextual I'm Stuck questions
Transparent 100-point activity completion, private history and portfolio exports
Mobile-responsive, no account or subscription, GitHub Pages ready
projects.notice: Curated educational models, not real-time engineering simulations or validated failure predictions. Activity completion is not a factual grade. Student work is stored privately in each visitor's own browser.

projects.title: Tech X-Ray
projects.tagline: See beyond the headline.
projects.description: An interactive technology literacy lab. Investigate emerging technologies by sorting their capabilities, dependencies, constraints and stakeholders, then uncover the hidden requirements behind each system.
projects.imageAlt: Tech X-Ray circular scanning diagram with capabilities, dependencies, constraints and stakeholders
overview: Tech X-Ray is a free, offline-first learning activity inspired by systems thinking and Contextual Adaptation in technological futures education. Start with an emerging technology, then separate what it can do from everything required to make it work.
Classify twelve evidence cards into four layers, identify three critical dependencies, and reflect on how the technology might operate in education, workplaces, communities or ecological contexts.
Finally, reveal three often-overlooked dependencies and compare your reasoning against a curated reference. Save attempts locally and export your work for a digital learning portfolio.
highlights: 12 emerging technologies with 144 curated evidence cards
Four X-Ray layers: capabilities, dependencies, constraints and stakeholders
36 intentionally hidden dependencies, revealed at the end
Drag-and-drop and accessible dropdown sorting
Select three critical dependencies and complete four contextual reflections
Transparent offline formative feedback out of 100, with explanations
Contextual I'm Stuck guidance without giving away answers
Private browser history, Markdown exports, JSON backup and restore
Responsive, GitHub Pages ready and free of accounts, subscriptions and API keys
projects.notice: An educational practice activity, not a technical audit. Scores measure reference classification and reflection completion, not factual accuracy. History is stored in each visitor's browser.

projects.title: Stillroom
projects.tagline: Your own quiet corner.
projects.description: Stillroom is a calm, offline notebook and rich-text writing application built in Python with PySide6. Capture ideas, organise notebooks, and write without accounts, subscriptions or cloud dependencies.
overview: Stillroom is a local-first writing space designed to reduce distractions. It offers a clean three-column layout, a comfortable editor and light and dark themes, bringing the familiar features of a notebook into a self-contained desktop application.

Instead of inserting Markdown symbols, Stillroom uses genuine rich-text editing for bold, italic, underline, headings, lists and quotations. Notes are automatically saved on the computer and can be searched by their content, title, notebook or tags.

Organise ideas into separate notebooks, favourite and pin important notes, archive finished work, and restore notes from Trash. Focus mode hides surrounding navigation so the writing page can take centre stage.
The app avoids accounts, analytics, cloud sync and background services. Export individual notes as HTML or text, or create a full JSON backup of your collection.
highlights: Native Python desktop application built with PySide6 and Qt6
Direct rich-text editing with bold, italic, underline, headings, lists and quotations
Paper-inspired writing canvas with light and dark themes
Notebooks, searchable tags, pinned notes and favourites
Full note search across titles, text, notebooks and tags
Focus mode for distraction-free writing
Archive, Trash and note restoration
Automatic local saving with migration and previous-save backups
Export notes as HTML or plain text and export all note data as JSON
Works offline after initial dependency installation with no account or background server
projects.notice: Stillroom 3.0.3 is a downloadable desktop Python application, not a browser app or GitHub Pages experience. Python 3.10+ and PySide6 are required; the Windows launcher installs PySide6 on first use. Notes are stored locally. The task button inserts a checkbox symbol rather than a functional checklist; cloud sync, encryption and attachments are not included.
